record.paper_title: Tree Spanners on Chordal Graphs: Complexity, Algorithms, Open Problems
record.original_question: For a chordal graph G, let r(G) be the radius of G and diam(G) be the diameter of G. Is there an efficient algorithm to decide, for chordal graphs satisfying diam(G) = 2r(G) - 2, whether G admits a tree (2r(G) - 1)-spanner, meaning a spanning tree T in which d_T(x, y) <= (2r(G) - 1)d_G(x, y) for every pair of vertices x and y?

evidence.quote: be decided efficiently on chordal graphs

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graph $G=(V,E)$ is chordal if every cycle of length at least 4 has a chord. For a connected graph $G$, let $d_G(x,y)$ denote the shortest-path distance between vertices $x$ and $y$, let the eccentricity of a vertex $v$ be $e_G(v)=\max_{u\in V} d_G(v,u)$, let the radius be $r(G)=\min_{v\in V} e_G(v)$, and let the diameter be $\operatorname{diam}(G)=\max_{v\in V} e_G(v)$. A spanning tree $T$ of $G$ is called a tree $t$-spanner of $G$ if $d_T(x,y)\le t\cdot d_G(x,y)$ for every pair of vertices $x,y\in V$.

Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a chordal graph $G$ satisfying $\operatorname{diam}(G)=2\,r(G)-2$, decides whether $G$ admits a tree $(2\,r(G)-1)$-spanner?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is equivalent to deciding whether chordal graphs of diameter 2 admit a tree 3-spanner, and the complexity of the Tree 3-Spanner problem on chordal graphs (even on strongly chordal undirected path graphs) is reported as still open in the literature on tree spanners of chordal graphs.

status_evidence.title: Tree spanners on chordal graphs: complexity and algorithms
status_evidence.snippet: Chordal graphs of diameter 2r(G)−2 admit tree (2r(G)−1)-spanners iff chordal graphs of diameter 2 admit tree 3-spanners; complexity of Tree 3-Spanner remains open for chordal graphs.
status_evidence.claim: The decision question is equivalent to the still-open Tree 3-Spanner problem on chordal graphs.

status_evidence.title: An Approximation Algorithm for the Tree t-Spanner Problem on Unweighted Graphs via Generalized Chordal Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses tree t-spanners on chordal-like graph classes; complexity of tree 3-spanner on chordal graphs is referenced as open.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature still references this complexity as open.
